chunks: 3285 - And al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar ibn Marwan, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, or he said: one of his companions asked him, about a man testifying for his father, or a brother for his brother, or a man for his wife.
He عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in that if he is righteous. His testimony is accepted for his father, and a father’s for his son, and a brother’s for his brother.”

key_terms.شَهَادَتُهُ: his testimony as evidence before judgment
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem or objection legally
key_terms.يَشْهَدُ: gives testimony or bears witness in a legal context

ai.seo_question: Is a man’s testimony accepted for his father, brother, or wife in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the acceptance of testimony among close family members. It indicates that such testimony is admissible when the witness is upright and good, specifically mentioning father, son, and brother. The report relates to judicial evaluation of witnesses rather than automatic rejection due to kinship alone.
